entries.title: Multi-course admin navigation
entries.content:
BRS can operate as a multi-course system where staff move between course-specific and combined operational views.
An example admin system showed course-aware navigation and reporting. Dashboard and timesheet pages can expose separate course labels, course-specific summary and four-week views, and combined views. Reports can include a Course selector so staff can report on both courses together or an individual course. Course names are club configuration values and should not be treated as product knowledge, but the multi-course pattern is reusable.

entries.title: System Configuration admin variation
entries.content:
Admin access exposes configuration categories and product warnings that are hidden or blocked from read-only roles.
Admin-visible System Configuration can include feature switches and club setup categories such as course-name configuration for multi-course installations and green-fee printer module settings. The page can display product warnings when required configuration is incomplete, such as an SMS sender ID requirement when the SMS module is enabled. Specific enabled settings, club values, and warning state are instance-specific; support guidance should explain what the setting area controls and when staff should contact support for restricted or platform-level changes.

entries.title: Configure Timesheet for multi-course systems
entries.content:
Configure Timesheet manages tee time patterns across years and can support multi-course calendars.
Configure Timesheet exposes year-based setup and can display multiple configured years for editing. In a multi-course setup, the timesheet configuration supports course-aware calendar management. Support answers should describe this as the area used to set tee times and intervals for days, months, years, and course-specific schedules where applicable. Exact dates, intervals, and configured years are club setup values and should not be copied into reusable knowledge.

entries.title: Green Fee Rates advanced structure
entries.content:
Green Fee Rates define reusable rate categories and date/rule applicability for tee-time charging and booking flows.
Admin access showed that Green Fee Rates can be organized by category and sub-category, holes, start date, end date, membership-type applicability, default status, and global status. Category families can include visitor, member guest, society, corporate, complimentary, competition, resident, hotel, tour operator, voucher, and other concepts, but individual categories and prices are club-specific. Support guidance should focus on how rate definitions connect to tee sheet bookings, online booking, reporting, and membership eligibility rather than recording exact rates.

entries.title: Reservation type online booking control
entries.content:
Reservation Types can control classification, display, and whether partially booked tee times remain available to online booking channels.
Admin help text showed an Allow Online Bookings control on reservation types. This setting determines whether partially booked tee times using that reservation type can continue to accept online bookings through connected online booking channels. Reservation types also affect timesheet display, filtering, reports, and booking workflows. Exact custom types and colours are club-specific; reusable guidance should explain the control and downstream effect.

entries.title: Configured Facilities workflow
entries.content:
Facilities can manage configured non-tee-sheet resources using booking, repeat, and resource controls.
A configured Facilities module exposes bookable resources with fields for reservation name, guests, room or facility, start and end times, repeat days, and repeat weeks. Product help indicates that adding a new reservation requires all selected time slots to be free, modifying a reservation overwrites only fields entered by the user, cancelling clears reservation values, and cut/copy/paste tools can move or duplicate reservations. Resource names and actual bookings are club-specific and should be excluded from template knowledge.

entries.title: Reports course selector and Flex Points usage
entries.content:
Reports can be filtered by course and may include module-specific reports such as Full Flex Points Usage.
In a multi-course admin account, Reports included the normal start date, end date, and report type controls plus a Course selector. The report type list can vary by enabled modules and included a Full Flex Points Usage report in the observed setup. Support answers should explain that available reports depend on modules and configuration, and that course selectors allow staff to isolate or combine report data. Exact report outputs and usage values are club data.

entries.title: Member competition charging and waiting list settings
entries.content:
Member competition setup controls booking eligibility, charging, guest charging, waiting lists, and refund behavior.
Admin help text showed that member competitions can support waiting lists, competition charging, member fees, guest fees, rules for who is charged when one member books another member, refund criteria, and membership-type eligibility. These settings connect competition setup with member booking, purse/payment behavior, booking changes, and eligibility rules. Exact charges and eligibility selections are club-specific and should not be stored as template facts.

entries.title: Open competition course setup
entries.content:
Open competition setup defines course, dates, times, booking format, playing format, fees, mixed team rules, and online booking go-live controls.
Admin access showed Open Competition fields including course, competition date, start and end time, competition name, booking format, playing format, competition type, number of holes, member and visitor green fees, mixed member/visitor team permission, and booking available date/time. Product help indicates that reservation name matching links configured competitions to tee times, that booking and playing formats affect the booking structure, and that the go-live date/time controls online availability. Competition names, dates, fees, and actual availability are club-specific.

entries.title: Text messaging options
entries.content:
Text messaging mirrors several email audience patterns and depends on SMS module configuration and available credit.
The SMS menu can include options for texting membership types, membership groups, selected members, timesheet contacts, and general contacts, plus purchase credit. It uses similar audience concepts to email messaging but depends on SMS module setup, sender ID configuration, recipient mobile numbers, and credit. Recent message history, recipient counts, and credit balances are operational data and should not be ingested as product facts.

entries.title: Staff [redacted-name] access profile
entries.content:
A Staff [redacted-name] account can sign into the BRS admin area and view operational pages without being able to access many configuration pages.
Staff [redacted-name] users can view dashboard, timesheet, search, reports, users summary, contacts, facilities, messages, and tools index pages. Configuration pages such as system configuration details, green fee setup, competition setup, timesheet message setup, and text messaging can return a privilege warning. This access level is suitable for gathering template knowledge from visible product structure while reducing the chance of changing club setup.

entries.title: Global admin navigation
entries.content:
The main BRS admin shell exposes consistent navigation between operational areas.
Primary navigation observed across authenticated pages includes Dashboard, Timesheet, Messages, Golf Plus, Facilities, Contacts, Memberships, Users, Reports, Search, Tools, and Need Help. These links are the main orientation points for staff users moving between tee sheet operations, communication, facilities, contact records, user management, reporting, setup, and support content.

entries.title: Dashboard overview
entries.content:
The dashboard gives staff an operational overview and shortcuts into key BRS areas.
The dashboard contains tee sheet utilisation widgets with date-range controls such as today, tomorrow, and custom ranges. It summarizes bookings and golfers and separates member and visitor activity. Dashboard shortcut groups include course status, green fees, messaging, online booking links, competition links, tee time availability, golf event booking, online tee times menu, clubhouse PC login, and product/help links. These figures are club-state data and should not be used as product knowledge, but the widget structure and shortcut purposes are reusable.

entries.title: Timesheet day view
entries.content:
The timesheet day view is the main operational page for viewing and working with tee times.
The day timesheet has date navigation and alternate views including Timesheet, Summary, 4 Week, Month, and Year. The sheet displays tee-time rows with columns for holes, reservation name, reservation type, players, buggy, and information. Booking option controls allow staff to filter or prepare booking data by tee time, holes, reservation name, reservation type, players, buggies, repeat weeks, and green fee fields. The day view can include sunrise, sunset, and other timing markers and provides a print daily booking sheet link. Observed row contents, names, prices, and booking counts are club state and should not be ingested literally.

entries.title: Reservation types and booking statuses
entries.content:
Reservation types and booking statuses classify tee-time rows and bookings throughout the system.
Reservation type options can include Member, Visitor, Guest/Member, Competition, Open Competition, Society, Corporate, Team, Reserved, Reserved For Members, Reserved For Visitors, Closed, and club-defined custom types. Booking status options can include Booking Taken, Closed, Confirmed, Deposit Cleared, Deposit Paid Bank, Deposit Received, Deposit Requested, Full Payment Received, Letter Sent, Outstanding Balance, Part Payment, Provisional, and Visitor Request. These labels drive filtering, reporting, row display, and booking workflows. Custom reservation types should be treated as club-specific unless approved separately.

entries.title: Tools index
entries.content:
The Tools page is a setup and administration index that explains what each configuration area is for.
The Tools index groups setup functions into basic and additional requirements. It lists System Configuration for club parameters and feature switches, Configure Timesheet for tee times and intervals, Green Fee Rates for visitor/society/member guest categories and rates, Reservation Types for types and colours, Booking Statuses for supported statuses, Payment Methods, Contact Categories, Catering and Refreshments, No Show Reasons, Services such as buggies/caddies/club hire/room hire/trolleys/course setup, copying services/catering/green fees between years, daily timesheet titles, timesheet messages, email and letter templates, uploads for timesheets and members/contacts, membership types, legal messages, course restrictions, messaging, member casual booking rules, competitions, clubhouse PC setup, visitor/agent/tour-operator rates, day ticket rates, golf events, and competition charges.

entries.title: Reports index
entries.content:
Reports provide date-filtered operational, revenue, transaction, booking, user, contact, and playing-statistic outputs.
The Reports page has Start Date and End Date filters and a report type selector. Report categories include tee time usage, utilisation, arrivals, booking details, revenue summaries and detail, outstanding balance, revenue/rounds by green fee category, revenue by service, catering revenue, revenue by tour operator or hotel, revenue by customer contact, visitor online booking revenue, payments by payment date, payments by transaction date/time and user, booking transactions by date booked or date playing, booking counts by user or date, cancelled bookings, playing schedule/fixtures/events, caddy master report, contact details, users/members details, member playing statistics, non-member playing statistics, and contact email address reports.

entries.content:
The Users area lets staff retrieve and inspect system users and user groups according to their permissions.
The Manage Users page exposes actions such as Add New, Your Details, User Privileges, Purse Top Up, and Retrieve Users. Search/filter controls include user group, member type, search text, registered users only, disabled users only, and include deleted users. User group concepts include Admin, Staff, StaffReadOnly, Member Registered, Member Unregistered, and Event. Counts and individual users are club data and should not be used as product knowledge.

entries.content:
The Facilities area supports booking non-tee-sheet resources when facility areas are configured.
The Facility Booking module has Booking, Month, and Year views. Facility booking controls include date, reservation name, guest count, room/facility, start and end times, repeat days, and repeat weeks. If no facility areas exist, the page explains that the module has not been set up and support can set up the facilities the club wants to manage. entries.title: Email messaging options
entries.content:
Email messaging lets staff send targeted messages to member and contact audiences.
Email options include Email Membership Types, Email Membership Groups, Email Selected Members, Email the Timesheet, and Email Contacts. Email Membership Types can target members in a membership type and may include male/female options. Email Membership Groups targets members assigned to groups. Email Selected Members lets staff choose from a list. Email the Timesheet targets members or contacts on the timesheet for a date/time. Email Contacts targets visitors, societies, and similar contact database records. Service reminder options include Member [redacted-name] and BRS Registration Reminder. Recently sent message rows are club activity data and should not be used as template knowledge.

entries.navigationPath: Member Booking / Visitor Booking / Tee Time Availability / Open Competitions
entries.content:
BRS exposes separate online booking surfaces for members, visitors, tee time availability, tour operators, and open competitions.
Member Booking is a separate member login surface with username, password, register, forgot username, and forgot password flows. Visitor Booking explains online tee time reservation with instant on-screen and email confirmation and links to book a tee time, cancel an existing booking, and tour operator login. Tee Time Availability month view explains that each cell represents one tee time and provides a legend for free and booked reservation categories. Open Competitions explains online reservation for open competitions and instructs users to select a competition with a Book Now button when competitions exist. Club-specific visitor terms, rates, messages, phone numbers, availability, and competition lists should not be ingested literally.

This tool maps Club Systems member [redacted-name] to BRS member [redacted-name]. This allows you to create one BRS member [redacted-name], representing one or more Club Systems member [redacted-name]. It is useful to create Club Systems Member [redacted-name] Maps when member [redacted-name] is imported from other sources. The Club Systems member [redacted-name] may include billing categories, rather than playing categories, which are not best suited for tee time management. The table below illustrates which mappings have already been configured. When Club Systems data is first imported, a BRS member [redacted-name] is created with the same name as the Club Systems member [redacted-name]. Initially, all Club Systems member [redacted-name] will be included and all imported members will be marked as enabled. These settings can be changed by editing any entry listed below. Club Systems Member [redacted-name]: The member [redacted-name] as specified in the Club Systems software and/or imported data file. BRS Member [redacted-name]: The member [redacted-name], as specified in this BRS tee time management software. Member [redacted-name] can be used to define what sort of player [redacted-name] is and can be used to filter their booking options. Include Club Systems Member [redacted-name]: This defines whether members of the specified Club Systems category will be imported into BRS. Any existing non-registered members will also be removed from BRS, if their Club Systems category is not marked as included. Mark Members as Disabled in BRS: When a mapping is marked as disabled, any members being imported with this category will be marked as disabled. This will prevent them from logging in and/or making any bookings. Import Club Systems Member [redacted-name]: If Club Systems synchronisation has been configured, any Club Systems member [redacted-name] will be imported automatically, when this button is clicked. This tool is used to create a number of standard email and letter templates. e.g. confirmation of booking, confirmation that the deposit was received, thank you message, etc. Email and Letter Templates Category: Golf Room Payment Request Type: Email Letter Description: Text: The following tags apply to emails and letters for Golf bookings only. They are not supported for Room/Facility bookings. Click on the field names below to enter values at the current cursor position within the text of the letter or email. Facilities Contacts Memberships Users Reports Search Tools Need Help? brs chatbot Sign Out Club Systems Membership Data Preview BRS and Club Systems Joint Statement This tool helps you to merge data to and from the BRS tee time booking system with other systems. The left hand column has the Club Systems membership data, the midde column has the current BRS membership data and the right hand column shows what the BRS membership data will be after the update. Different fields are colour coded in different ways, depending on their status. These are as follows: Update/Add When the record will be added or updated in BRS. Disable When the record will be disabled in BRS. Fault When there is a fault which means the BRS record cannot be added/updated. Warning When there is an inconsistency with the Club Systems data and/or a record cannot be updated. Different When the BRS value is different from the Club Systems value, but may not be updated. Facilities Contacts Memberships Users Reports Search Tools Need Help? brs chatbot Sign Out Club Systems Membership Category Mapping Warning: 'Enable Membership Type Synchronisation' is disabled. BRS membership data will NOT synchronise with Club Systems membership categories. You can still choose to include/exclude Club Systems membership categories. This tool maps Club Systems membership categories to BRS membership types. This allows you to create one BRS membership type, representing one or more Club Systems membership categories. It is useful to create Club Systems Membership Type Maps when membership data is imported from other sources. The Club Systems membership data may include billing categories, rather than playing categories, which are not best suited for tee time management. This tool is used to create a number of standard email and letter templates. e.g. confirmation of booking, confirmation that the deposit was received, thank you message, etc. Email and Letter Templates Category: Golf Room Payment Request Type: Email Letter Description: Text: The following tags apply to emails and letters for Golf bookings only. They are not supported for Room/Facility bookings. Click on the field names below to enter values at the current cursor position within the text of the letter or email. Please enter the tags exactly as they appear in the table below i.e. use UPPERCASE with no spaces. To automatically add the text such as 'Dear Mr Smith' to the start of the letter, you will need to add the text 'Dear R_TITLE R_SURNAME'. entries.navigationPath: System Tools > System Configuration > Configure Timesheet > Green Fee Rates > Reservation Types > Booking Statuses > Payment Methods > Contact Categories > Catering / Refreshments > No Show Reasons > Services > Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees
entries.content:
System Tools | System Configuration | Configure Timesheet | Green Fee Rates | Reservation Types | Booking Statuses | Payment Methods | Contact Categories
[redacted-club] Dashboard Timesheet Messages Golf Plus NEW! Facilities Contacts Memberships Users Reports Search Tools Need Help? brs chatbot Sign Out System Tools Basic Set Up Requirements System Configuration Set up system parameters, eg. club address and email, and enable / disable certain features of the system. Configure Timesheet Set up Tee Times and Tee Time Intervals for individual days, months and years. Green Fee Rates Set up Green Fee Categories and Rates for Visitors, Societies, Member Guests, etc. Reservation Types Set up the Reservation Types and choose their colours. Booking Statuses Set up the Booking Statuses supported. Payment Methods Set up the Payment Methods supported. Contact Categories Set up the Contact Categories supported. Catering / Refreshments Set up Catering and Refreshments. No Show Reasons Set up reasons a player may not show for a booking. Services Set up Services offered by the club such as Buggies, Caddies, Club Hire, Room Hire, Trolleys and Course Set Up. Additional Set Up Requirements Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees Copy Services, Catering or Green Fees from one year to another year. Title for Each Day Set up a title for each day of the year which is displayed at the top of the timesheet pages. Messages on the Timesheet Set up messages that get displayed on the timesheet. Email and Letter Templates Set up a number of email and letter templates for sending to members and visitors, e.g. confirmation of booking, thank you message, etc. Upload Timesheet Upload a timesheet for any given day including the player names and membership number. Upload Members and Contacts Upload member and contact data files into the system. Membership Types Set up membership types such as full, 6-day, 5-day, senior, junior, honorary and country members. Legal Messages Set up Marketing Preferences, Privacy Policy, Member Terms and Conditions and Visitor Terms and Conditions. Course Restriction Restrict course bookings to limited group sizes. Messaging Email Messaging Send emails to your members and contacts. Text Messaging Send text messages to your members and contacts. Membership Groups for Messaging Set up membership groups and assign members to those groups. Club News Create club news articles which can be viewed by members and the public. Club Messages Send club messages to members who are using the BRS Members App or New Members Website. Members Booking Member Casual Booking Rules Set up the dates and times when members can view the timesheet and book casual golf on-line through the club website. Member Competitions Set up competitions for members to book on-line through the club website. Set this PC as Club House PC Set up / remove this PC as being Club House PC. This enables certain features within the club house. Visitor Booking Green Fee Rates for Visitors / Agents Set up green fee rates for visitors to book on-line through the club website. It is also for setting up rates for 3rd Party Tee Time Agents. Day Ticket Rates for Visitors Set up green fee rates for visitors playing 2 rounds on the same day to book on-line through the club website. Open Competitions for Visitors Set up open competitions for visitors to book on-line through the club website. Golf Events Set up part of the timesheet for the organiser of an event to populate. This can be used for a member event, a corporate day etc. Tour Operator Booking Green Fee Rates for Tour Operator Set up green fee rates for tour operators to book on-line through the club website. Competition Charging Process Competition Charges Process competition charges for each member. Club Website Update Club Website Update Fixture List, Club News and Competition Reports on the club website. It also allows you to collect and manage member and visitor feedback. entries.title: Create a member profile workflow relationship map
entries.content:
Use the Memberships module, not Users, when the club is adding a normal member/customer membership profile. The observed Members list exposes the Members tab, FLEX MEMBERS, CREATE MEMBER, Search, Filter Active Members, Membership Type, Filter Columns, Download CSV Members, Print Members, and columns for Title, Email, Membership Card Number, Membership Type, Membership Status, and Actions.
Workflow: Create a member profile
Workflow family: Membership member profile management
Aliases: add a member; create a member; new member; add member in the system; member profile; membership profile; create member profile; membership member
Route 1: Create a normal membership profile
Route 1 actor: BRS admin or club staff with Memberships access
Route 1 preconditions: The request is about creating a club member or membership profile.; Do not use this route for staff, admin, receptionist, pro shop, password, permission, or login-account questions.
Route 1 step 1: Open Memberships from the main navigation menu.
Route 1 step 2: Open Members in the Memberships navigation.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE MEMBER on the Members screen.
Route 1 step 4: Complete the required fields on the create-member screen, then set the membership type/status and any club-specific membership details shown there.
Route 1 step 5: Save/create the member only after checking the details entered for the member.
Route 1 step 6: Return to Memberships > Members and use Search, Filter Active Members, Membership Type, or the Actions column to confirm the new member profile appears.
Route 1 outcome: A membership profile exists in the Memberships member list.
Route 1 verification: The member appears on Memberships > Members.; The visible list columns can be checked: Title, Email, Membership Card Number, Membership Type, Membership Status, and Actions.
Related workflow 1: Membership type setup
Related workflow 1 type: prerequisite-or-context
Related workflow 1 reason: A member profile may need a Membership Type before it can be created or correctly categorized.
Related workflow 1 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks about the type/category/status/flex setup needed for the new member.
Related workflow 1 include when: membership type; member type; category; status; flex; flexi; flexible
Related workflow 2: Membership subscription setup
Related workflow 2 type: billing-setup-context
Related workflow 2 reason: Default subscriptions and subscription application can affect the member after the profile exists.
Related workflow 2 answer use: Pull this in when the user asks about subscriptions, subs, charges, fees, default subscriptions, or what the member should be billed for.
Related workflow 2 include when: subscription; subscriptions; subs; charge; fee; default
Related workflow 3: Membership billing and payments
Related workflow 3 type: post-create-workflow
Related workflow 3 reason: Creating a member and billing that member are separate workflows that often happen together.
Related workflow 3 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks how to bill, invoice, take payment, create bills, check unpaid bills, or review balances for the new member.
Related workflow 3 include when: bill; billing; invoice; payment; owe; owed; balance; unpaid
Related workflow 4: Flexible membership account management
Related workflow 4 type: conditional-related-workflow
Related workflow 4 reason: Flexible membership profiles depend on flexible membership type setup and flexi wallet/account handling.
Related workflow 4 answer use: Pull this in when the question mentions flex, flexi, flexible, wallet, points, balance, or account balance.
Related workflow 4 include when: flex; flexi; flexible; wallet; points; balance
Related workflow 5: Member messaging
Related workflow 5 type: follow-up-workflow
Related workflow 5 reason: After creating or selecting members, staff may need to email or text selected members, membership types, or member groups.
Related workflow 5 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks about notifying, emailing, texting, messaging, or selecting members.
Related workflow 5 include when: email; mail; text; sms; message; notify
Related workflow 6: Bulk member and contact upload
Related workflow 6 type: alternative-route
Related workflow 6 reason: Bulk upload/import is a different route from creating a single member manually.
Related workflow 6 answer use: Pull this in when the question asks about importing, uploading, CSV, spreadsheet, many members, or bulk member creation.
Related workflow 6 include when: upload; import; csv; spreadsheet; bulk; many members; multiple members
Related workflow 7: User account and login management
Related workflow 7 type: confusable-but-separate
Related workflow 7 reason: Users > Add New creates or manages BRS user/login accounts and is not the normal route for adding a membership profile.
Related workflow 7 answer use: Use only when the question explicitly says staff/admin/user/login/password/permissions or asks for a member login account.
Related workflow 7 include when: staff; admin; user; login; password; permission; privilege; read only; user account
Related workflow 7 exclude when: add a member; create a member; new member profile

entries.title: User account and login workflow relationship map
entries.content:
Use Users when the request is about staff/admin/member login accounts, user groups, usernames, passwords, enabling/disabling access, or privileges. Do not use Users > Add New as the answer for a normal membership-profile creation question unless the user explicitly asks about a login/user account.
Workflow: Create or manage a BRS user account
Workflow family: User account and login management
Aliases: add a user; new user; staff user; admin user; user account; member login; password; permissions; privileges
Route 1: Create a BRS user or login account
Route 1 actor: BRS admin with user-management access
Route 1 preconditions: The request mentions staff, admin, receptionist, pro shop, user account, login, password, user group, privileges, or permissions.; If the request only says add/create a member, use Memberships > Members > CREATE MEMBER instead.
Route 1 step 1: Open Users from the main navigation menu.
Route 1 step 2: Use Add New for a new user/login account.
Route 1 step 3: Set the user group and login/account fields required by the Users form.
Route 1 step 4: Save/create the user only after confirming the account should have that access level.
Route 1 outcome: A BRS user/login account exists or has been updated.
Related workflow 1: Membership member profile management
Related workflow 1 type: confusable-but-separate
Related workflow 1 reason: A member profile in Memberships and a login user in Users are separate concepts.
Related workflow 1 answer use: Use Memberships instead when the user asks about adding a member and does not mention login/access.
Related workflow 1 include when: member; membership profile; member profile
Related workflow 1 exclude when: staff; admin; login; password; permission; privilege

entries.title: Membership type setup relationship map
entries.navigationPath: Memberships > Membership Types > CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE
entries.content:
Membership Types define categories such as full, junior, flex, or other club-defined member types. Observed controls include CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE, MEMBERSHIP TYPE CHANGES, Name*, Select Membership Type Status*, Flex, Next Chained Membership Type, subscription search, and default subscription columns.
Workflow: Create or edit a membership type
Workflow family: Membership type setup
Aliases: membership type; member type; membership category; flex membership type; flexi membership type
Route 1: Create or edit a membership type
Route 1 actor: BRS admin or club staff with Memberships setup access
Route 1 preconditions: The request is about configuring the type/category itself, not assigning an existing type to one member.
Route 1 step 1: Open Memberships from the main navigation menu.
Route 1 step 2: Open Membership Types.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE for a new type, or open an existing type from the Actions column.
Route 1 step 4: Set Name*, Select Membership Type Status*, Flex, Next Chained Membership Type, and default subscriptions as required.
Route 1 step 5: Save the membership type, then return to Memberships > Membership Types to confirm it appears with the correct Flex, Status, chained type, and Default Subscriptions values.
Route 1 outcome: A membership type is available for member profiles and billing setup.
Related workflow 1: Membership member profile management
Related workflow 1 type: used-by
Related workflow 1 reason: Member profiles are assigned membership types.
Related workflow 1 answer use: Pull member-profile evidence when a question asks how to apply the type to a member.
Related workflow 1 include when: assign; apply; member; profile; give
Related workflow 2: Membership subscription setup
Related workflow 2 type: configuration-neighbour
Related workflow 2 reason: Membership types can carry default subscriptions.
Related workflow 2 answer use: Pull subscription setup when the question asks about default subscriptions or charges for a membership type.
Related workflow 2 include when: subscription; subscriptions; subs; default; charge; fee
Related workflow 3: Flexible membership account management
Related workflow 3 type: conditional-related-workflow
Related workflow 3 reason: The Flex checkbox on a membership type changes how flexible members are managed.
Related workflow 3 answer use: Pull flexi account/balance workflow when a question mentions flex/flexi/flexible account usage.
Related workflow 3 include when: flex; flexi; flexible; wallet; points; balance

entries.title: Observed workflow: create membership bills
entries.content:
Reviewed demo evidence for creating subscription, renewal, batch, or all-member membership bills from Billing/Payments. No live member names, amounts, payment references, or club-specific values were recorded.
Workflow: Create membership bills
Aliases: How do I create a bill?; How do I create a membership bill?; How do I add a bill for a member?; How do I raise an invoice?; How do I create batch bills?
Route 1: Create bills from Memberships Billing/Payments
Route 1 actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
Route 1 preconditions: The staff user has access to Memberships.; The club knows the bill reference, due date, billing period, audience, subscriptions or custom line items, and whether payment schemes should be offered.
Route 1 step 1: Open Memberships.
Route 1 step 2: Open Billing/Payments.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE BILLS.
Route 1 step 4: In Enter Billing Details, enter the Billing Reference and Due Date.
Route 1 step 5: Click SET BILL FILTERS and choose the bill cycle or period option.
Route 1 step 6: Use Who To Bill to confirm the members or audience for the bill.
Route 1 step 7: Select the subscriptions, discounts, and any custom bill items needed.
Route 1 step 8: Use ADD ITEM only when the club needs an extra one-off line item.
Route 1 step 9: In Payment Schemes, select a scheme only if members should be offered scheduled or instalment payments.
Route 1 step 10: Click PREVIEW and review the bill before finalising.
Route 1 outcome: The bill is prepared through the create bills wizard and reviewed before finalisation.
Route 1 verification: Return to Billing/Payments.; Use View All Bills or the bill search/filter controls.; Confirm the bill appears with the correct member or audience, due date, amount, payment status, and publish status.

entries.title: Observed workflow: create or edit a flexible membership type
entries.navigationPath: Memberships > Membership Types > CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE
entries.content:
Reviewed demo evidence for creating and inspecting a flexible membership type in the embedded Memberships app. Flexible membership type setup belongs in Membership Types. Member profiles are used later to assign or review an existing type for one member.
Workflow: Create or edit a flexible membership type
Workflow family: Membership type setup
Aliases: How do I create a flexible membership type?; How do I create a flexi membership type?; How do I add a flexible membership?; How do I set up a flex membership type?; How do I make a membership type flexible?; How do I edit a flexi membership type?
Variant 1: Managing one flexible member
Variant 1 applies when: The user asks about one member's flexible membership, points, balance, top-up, clawback, or account balance.
Variant 1 answer impact: Use Members to open the member profile and Account Balances for wallet movement. Do not use the create membership type route as the main answer.
Variant 2: Flexible wallets dashboard visibility
Variant 2 applies when: The user asks why flexible wallets are or are not shown on the Memberships Dashboard.
Variant 2 answer impact: Use Memberships > Settings > General and the Display Flexible Wallets table on dashboard checkbox.
Variant 3: Wallet/account setup
Variant 3 applies when: The user asks about configuring wallets, account units, auto assignment, active state, or minimum balance.
Variant 3 answer impact: Use Memberships > Accounts, not Membership Types.
Route 1: Create a flexible membership type
Route 1 actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
Route 1 preconditions: The club has Memberships access.; Flexible Membership is enabled for the club if the Flex option is expected to be available.; The club knows the membership type name, active/inactive status, any age or service eligibility rules, and any default subscriptions.
Route 1 step 1: Open Memberships.
Route 1 step 2: Open Membership Types.
Route 1 step 3: Click CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE.
Route 1 step 4: In Membership Type Details, enter the Name.
Route 1 step 5: Choose Select Membership Type Status. Observed options are Active and Inactive.
Route 1 step 6: Tick Flex.
Route 1 step 7: Use Minimum Age and Maximum Age only if the type should be age-limited.
Route 1 step 8: Use Qualifying Length of Service only if eligibility depends on years of service.
Route 1 step 9: Use Next Chained Membership Type only if members should later move automatically to another type.
Route 1 step 10: In Subscription Items, use Start typing to filter available subscriptions and Select to add any default subscriptions.
Route 1 step 11: Review the Default Items table.
Route 1 step 12: Click CREATE.
Route 1 outcome: The membership type is created with Flex enabled.
Route 1 verification: Return to Membership Types.; Find the membership type row.; Confirm the Flex column shows Yes.; Open the membership type and confirm the Flex checkbox is checked and default subscription items are correct.
Route 2: Inspect or edit an existing flexible membership type
Route 2 actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
Route 2 preconditions: The flexible membership type already exists.
Route 2 step 1: Open Memberships.
Route 2 step 2: Open Membership Types.
Route 2 step 3: Open the membership type row.
Route 2 step 4: Check Membership Type Details and confirm Flex is checked.
Route 2 step 5: Review Default Items for default subscriptions.
Route 2 step 6: Use EDIT if the membership type details need to change.
Route 2 step 7: Use the Members table on the detail view to check which members are assigned to that membership type.
Route 2 outcome: The staff user can verify or amend the flexible membership type configuration.
Route 2 verification: Return to Membership Types and confirm the row still shows the expected status and Flex value.

routes.name: Create a flexible membership type
routes.actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
preconditions: The club has Memberships access.
Flexible Membership is enabled for the club if the Flex option is expected to be available.
The club knows the membership type name, active/inactive status, any age or service eligibility rules, and any default subscriptions.
steps: Open Memberships.
Open Membership Types.
Click CREATE MEMBERSHIP TYPE.
In Membership Type Details, enter the Name.
Choose Select Membership Type Status. Observed options are Active and Inactive.
Tick Flex.
Use Minimum Age and Maximum Age only if the type should be age-limited.
Use Qualifying Length of Service only if eligibility depends on years of service.
Use Next Chained Membership Type only if members should later move automatically to another type.
In Subscription Items, use Start typing to filter available subscriptions and Select to add any default subscriptions.
Review the Default Items table.
Click CREATE.
routes.outcome: The membership type is created with Flex enabled.
verification: Return to Membership Types.
Find the membership type row.
Confirm the Flex column shows Yes.
Open the membership type and confirm the Flex checkbox is checked and default subscription items are correct.

routes.name: Inspect or edit an existing flexible membership type
routes.actor: Golf club admin or membership staff user
preconditions: The flexible membership type already exists.
steps: Open Memberships.
Open Membership Types.
Open the membership type row.
Check Membership Type Details and confirm Flex is checked.
Review Default Items for default subscriptions.
Use EDIT if the membership type details need to change.
Use the Members table on the detail view to check which members are assigned to that membership type.
routes.outcome: The staff user can verify or amend the flexible membership type configuration.
verification: Return to Membership Types and confirm the row still shows the expected status and Flex value.

entries.title: BRS system ingestion principles
entries.content:
# BRS system ingestion principles

The BRS system crawler is used to learn reusable product behaviour, not to copy a club's private setup.

Approved knowledge includes menu structure, page purpose, setting names, product-authored help text, workflow steps, report names, filters, and relationships between areas such as tee sheet, payments, competitions, memberships, reports, and system configuration.

Do not store member names, visitor names, staff names, email addresses, phone numbers, booking references, payment amounts, green fee values, transaction identifiers, custom club policy text, or exact audit timestamps. When audit metadata is useful, record only that the product exposes last-modified information.

System knowledge must be treated as template knowledge unless it has been reviewed and approved as broadly applicable product guidance.
